text:
priya: FYI I ran into a confusing UX while teaching the Go quickstart to a customer. Our generator Stream API requires callers to manage Close(), but Close only closes the chunk channel; internal goroutines (handshake/auth) can still keep the process alive if they never see cancel.

priya: Repro pattern I used in the workshop: start an http.Handler that kicks off a stream in a goroutine and returns. Students expected the handler return to be enough for lambda-style runtimes. Sometimes the function kept hanging 1-3s after handler return.

priya: Short snippet we show in docs:```go
func chatHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request){
 ctx := r.Context()
 g := client.Generator("redwood/mini")
 s, _ := g.Stream(ctx, prompt)
 defer s.Close()
 go func(){
   for chunk := range s.Chunks(){
     w.Write(chunk)
   }
 }()
 return
}
```

tony: This is subtle and worth fixing. Two separate issues: (1) internal handshake goroutine needs to watch ctx.Done(); (2) auth/token refresh path currently blocks on a dedupe lock while performing network I/O, so even if ctx is cancelled the fetch can continue holding resources.

kevin: To keep API ergonomic we could add StreamWithContext(ctx) and also make Stream(ctx) semantics explicit in docs. But adding a new API surface requires semver considerations and a compatibility shim for existing callers.

priya: I tried a tiny repro where the handshake goroutine sleeps for 2s (no ctx check) and the handler returns immediately. The test runner reported stuck goroutines. Adding `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 500*time.Millisecond); defer cancel()` in handler made the behavior deterministic. But we shouldn't force every user to do that.

kevin: Implementation plan proposal:
- Propagate ctx into handshake/http requests and select on ctx.Done() when waiting for responses.
- Token refresh: change dedupe to optimistic double-check locking: acquire lock, check cached token; if refresh needed, mark in-flight, release lock, perform network call with ctx, reacquire lock and set token. That prevents holding a lock across network I/O.
- Add minimal StreamWithContext(ctx) shim that wires the provided ctx to internal ops. Keep Stream(ctx) unchanged for now but document that ctx is observed by internal operations.

sophia: Tests we should add: small unit that spawns Stream, cancels ctx, and asserts all goroutines exit within N ms. Integration test that simulates token endpoint sleeping and verifies cancel triggers early return. Also add a quickstart snippet showing recommended pattern for http handlers (block until stream completes or use explicit short timeout).

priya: For docs, suggest a short note: "Prefer StreamWithContext or explicitly call context.WithCancel on r.Context and cancel on handler exit. Avoid starting long-lived background goroutines that read stream without observing ctx." Add example.

ci-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-1701: "go sdk: stream handshake & auth should observe ctx; provide StreamWithContext shim". Linking tests/tasks: unit-cancel, integ-auth-slow.

kevin: On parity: JS has AbortSignal, Python libs commonly accept a timeout or rely on request session cancellation. Let's call out parity in the SDK docs and show equivalent snippets for each.

priya: I'll open a small PR with the handshake ctx select and token refresh lock rework + tests. Will add the StreamWithContext shim behind a minor feature flag so we can roll out without breaking. Assign reviewers kevin/sophia.

tony: Great. Also consider adding a low-friction helper `StreamCancelable` that returns (stream, cancelFunc) for users who prefer not threading contexts. But keep it as fallback to avoid API bloat.

priya: Thanks all — I'll post PR link once ready. ci-bot: DEVEX-1701 now has a PR draft attached.

priya: follow-up: merged the handshake ctx + token refresh fix, added unit tests. stream-with-context shim merged behind flag; docs updated. Canary run looks good.

ci-bot: DEVEX-1701 closed after successful canary.
